<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep Anthropic inline system reminders out of the leading prompt prefix when a template requires system-first ordering. Addresses #53393; refreshed against main `7b77ed581d` with the current renderer detection preserved.

## Claims

- Convert inline system text to user content in place on the existing system-first fallback and merge adjacent user messages; accepting templates retain inline system roles.
- Preserve the upstream conditional HF-template warning hint, update the existing `/v1/messages/render` regression, and document the automatic fallback and role-framing tradeoff in the Claude Code integration guide.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -q --tb=short` — **135 passed, 3 failed**. All three failures are `test_probes_non_jinja_renderer` cases requiring uncached DeepSeek model configurations; the same cases also fail on unmodified main `7b77ed581d` in this environment.
- The three `TestInlineSystemMessageMerge` regressions pass with the fix. With the PR's tests copied into a main control worktree and main production code unchanged, `... -k TestInlineSystemMessageMerge -q --tb=short` produces **3 failed**: main still hoists the reminder into the leading system prompt rather than retaining its position.
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -k messages_render_preserves_inline_system_position -q --tb=short` — **1 setup error** because `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`'s tokenizer is not cached and the download could not complete. No render assertion result is claimed. The existing test now compares exact token IDs against an equivalent in-place user-content request. Both test files are selected by `.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml`.
- Pre-commit on the four PR files and `git diff --check origin/main` — **passed**. Tool downloads required authenticated GitHub API retrieval with pinned commit/tree hash verification; project hook configuration was unchanged.
- New-head DCO passed. Remote pre-commit and the ReadTheDocs preview were not run because `pre-run-check` failed the contributor-eligibility gate (one merged PR); this is separate from the passing local checks. Fresh-agent discovery from the local checkout and GitHub PR branch found the new docs; the rendered-preview check could not complete because [the docs build was skipped](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35544200/).
- No fresh model/serving evaluation ran here; CUDA cannot initialize. [Community testing at the previous head `8c25637`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53501#issuecomment-6186232341) found an offline shared-prefix improvement from 77.8% to 100% on captured Claude Code/Qwen3.8 traffic. This was conversion/rendering, not live validation of this refreshed head. Earlier middleware production measurements also did not execute this patch.

## Details

Hoisting each per-turn reminder into the leading system block changes the prompt prefix on every request. This fallback preserves the reminder's text and conversation position but changes its role framing to user; it does not preserve system-level instruction priority. Current-head tool/reasoning compatibility and live serving validation remain outstanding.

Overlap check: open **#63368** targets the same prefix-cache problem by folding inline text into adjacent user/tool content, including structured tool-result handling. That differs materially from this PR's re-role/adjacent-user fallback and may better preserve some templates' reasoning history. Open Draft **#58772** proposes a broader preserve/fold normalizer and policy. Maintainer guidance is needed on which approach to take or consolidate; no independent-scope or merge-readiness claim is made. #58754 improved template detection but did not remove the rejecting-template fallback; #52978/#47681 use different merge policies.

Open since 2026-08-24. AI assistance was used for this refresh; signed-off, signed commits include Codex attribution. Human review and current-head model validation remain required.

nodes.body: Hello @DarkLight1337 @robertgshaw2-redhat @aarnphm @NickLucche @AndreasKaratzas @mgoin, when you have a chance, could you please review this PR? It preserves prefix-cache behavior for inline system turns. Any feedback or guidance on the implementation and test coverage would be greatly appreciated. Thank you for your time!

Tested the same transformation (inline system -> user in place) in production on Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 / vLLM v0.28.0 with Claude Code 2.1.296, via a request-rewriting middleware rather than this patch. Second request of a session: prefix-cache hits 14,112/20,068 -> 18,816/20,083, TTFT 1.9 s -> 0.48 s. Over 7 days before the change the aggregate hit rate was 31% with mean TTFT 19.5 s. Setup and numbers in #53393.

The patch no longer applies on main after #58754 (`_should_merge_inline_system` and the renderer changes). Do you plan to rebase? Happy to help test.

Hi @mgoin @NickLucche @chaunceyjiang @aarnphm @AndreasKaratzas @DarkLight1337 @robertgshaw2-redhat, I merged main `c5f8adc0`, retained #58754's resolved-template detection/current renderer API, and updated the startup warning to describe the actual in-place user-role fallback. The description now records the current PR checklist, signed-off/AI attribution, tests and model-validation limits.

Validation: **111 conversion tests passed**, with **15 inline-system tests** rerun after the warning update; the three fallback regressions fail on main. The production middleware results reported by wndaasa support the direction but did not test this head.

Open since **August 24**, this still affects rejecting templates because main continues to hoist their per-turn reminders into the leading prefix. Draft **#58772 overlaps** and proposes broader normalization/tool-result handling; this PR keeps the narrower existing fallback. Could you please review the updated diff and advise whether to advance this small fix or consolidate into #58772? Current-head tool/reasoning/model validation is still needed. Thank you.

Tested the current head (8c25637) offline against captured Claude Code 2.1.296 traffic, rendered through the Qwen3.8-27B template.

Setup: `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .` at 8c25637, Python 3.12. Two consecutive requests from one session (first user turn, then the same conversation after a tool call) converted with `to_chat_completion_request(merge_inline_system=True)` and rendered with `apply_chat_template` (tools included, `reasoning_effort="medium"`). `_detect_merge_inline_system` returns True for the stock Qwen3.8 template, so this exercises the fallback path.

- main (c5f8adc0): request 2 shares 15,430 of request 1's 19,841 tokens (77.8%). The divergence is inside the leading system block, where the per-turn `<total_tokens>` reminder gets appended.
- this PR: request 2 shares all 19,841 tokens (100%); request 1's rendered prompt is an exact prefix of request 2, and the reminder renders as a trailing `user` turn after the tool results (roles: system, user, assistant, tool, tool, user).
- `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`: 111 passed (15 inline-system cases).

This is conversion + rendering only, not a live run of this head against the model. The live numbers in #53393 came from the same transformation applied by a request-rewriting middleware in front of v0.28.0 (97.6% prefix-cache hit rate over 126 real requests, mean TTFT 0.83 s, versus 31% / 19.5 s before).

Thank you @wndaasa for testing `8c25637` with captured traffic and the Qwen3.8 template, and for rerunning the 111 tests. The shared-prefix improvement from 77.8% to 100%, with tools included, is useful validation of the fallback on this head.

I also appreciate your clearly separating the conversion/rendering test from the earlier middleware production measurements. Live model validation of this head, including tool/reasoning behavior, remains outstanding. Thanks again for taking the time to help test this!

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ActiveSky.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Hi @DarkLight1337 @robertgshaw2-redhat @chaunceyjiang, I have resolved the new conflict and merged main `7b77ed581d` in signed commit `1c45986d8109`. The refresh retains upstream's renderer detection and conditional HF-template hint, updates the existing `/v1/messages/render` regression for in-place reminder content, and adds the fallback/role-framing explanation to the Claude Code docs. The description and checklist now reflect current requirements and limitations.

Validation: pre-commit passed on all four PR files. The conversion suite has **135 passed, 3 failed**; those three cases need uncached DeepSeek configurations and fail identically on unmodified main. The three fallback regressions fail on main and pass here. The real render API regression is blocked at setup by the unavailable tiny tokenizer, and current-head live model/tool/reasoning validation is still outstanding.

On the new head, DCO passed, while remote pre-commit was skipped after `pre-run-check` stopped at the contributor-eligibility gate (one merged PR). This is separate from the local checks above; no remote code-test pass is claimed.

This PR has been open since **August 24**, and main still hoists inline reminders into the leading system block, disturbing the reusable prefix. I also found the newer overlapping **#63368**, whose user/tool-folding approach differs from this re-role fallback; **#58772** remains relevant too. Could you please prioritize a review or consolidation decision when possible, and advise which remaining validation would let the chosen fix proceed toward merge? Thank you for your time and help resolving this long-standing issue.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@@ -73,6 +73,19 @@ If the model responds correctly, your setup is working. You can now use Claude C
 
 ## Troubleshooting
 
+### Inline system messages and prefix caching
+
+The Anthropic frontend automatically checks whether the model's chat template
+accepts system messages after the first turn. For system-first templates, inline
+system text is converted to user content in place, and adjacent user messages are
+merged. Per-turn reminders therefore stay out of the leading system prompt,
+preserving its unchanged prefix for [prefix caching](../../design/prefix_caching.md).
+Templates that accept inline system messages retain their system roles.
+
+This fallback preserves the text and its position but changes its role framing;
+it does not preserve system-level instruction priority. Tool and reasoning
+behavior still depends on the model and template.
+
 **Connection refused**: Ensure vLLM is running and accessible at the specified URL. Check that the port matches.
 
 **Tool calls not working**: Verify that your model supports tool calling and that you've enabled it with the correct `--tool-call-parser` flag. See [Tool Calling](../../features/tool_calling.md).

+class TestInlineSystemMessageMerge:
+    def test_inline_system_is_rerolled_and_merged_with_user_turns(self):

+

+                "role": "user",

+                ],
+            }
+        ]
+

Tested the current head (8c25637) offline against captured Claude Code 2.1.296 traffic, rendered through the Qwen3.8-27B template.

Setup: `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .` at 8c25637, Python 3.12. Two consecutive requests from one session (first user turn, then the same conversation after a tool call) converted with `to_chat_completion_request(merge_inline_system=True)` and rendered with `apply_chat_template` (tools included, `reasoning_effort="medium"`). `_detect_merge_inline_system` returns True for the stock Qwen3.8 template, so this exercises the fallback path.

- main (c5f8adc0): request 2 shares 15,430 of request 1's 19,841 tokens (77.8%). The divergence is inside the leading system block, where the per-turn `<total_tokens>` reminder gets appended.
- this PR: request 2 shares all 19,841 tokens (100%); request 1's rendered prompt is an exact prefix of request 2, and the reminder renders as a trailing `user` turn after the tool results (roles: system, user, assistant, tool, tool, user).
- `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`: 111 passed (15 inline-system cases).

This is conversion + rendering only, not a live run of this head against the model. The live numbers in #53393 came from the same transformation applied by a request-rewriting middleware in front of v0.28.0 (97.6% prefix-cache hit rate over 126 real requests, mean TTFT 0.83 s, versus 31% / 19.5 s before).

Thank you @wndaasa for testing `8c25637` with captured traffic and the Qwen3.8 template, and for rerunning the 111 tests. The shared-prefix improvement from 77.8% to 100%, with tools included, is useful validation of the fallback on this head.

I also appreciate your clearly separating the conversion/rendering test from the earlier middleware production measurements. Live model validation of this head, including tool/reasoning behavior, remains outstanding. Thanks again for taking the time to help test this!
